solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Short and detached musical rejected by old Censor?

indicators.note: something rejected is thrown back, so the musical's name is read backwards

parts.note: Cats is the Lloyd Webber musical
Cato the Elder held the Roman office of censor

explanation.surface: A historical Roman moralist turns down a stage show for being too abrupt and aloof.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old Censor' hides a name: Cato the Elder, the Roman magistrate famous as 'the Censor'. 'rejected' reads the show's title backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Musical term for notes played sharply cut off and separated from one another.

clue.text: Short wacky girl going round that African country

indicators.note: the girl's name surrounds the shortened word
the word for wacky loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A short, eccentric girl travels around an African land.
explanation.definitionFit: East African nation formed from Tanganyika and Zanzibar.

clue.text: Female supporting auto sales place in Welsh town

indicators.note: in a down entry the female piece holds up the others from below

parts.note: a hen is a female bird

explanation.surface: A woman backing a used-car dealership in a Welsh town.
explanation.definitionFit: County town of Carmarthenshire in south-west Wales.

clue.text: Rating fools soldiers in outskirts of seaport

indicators.note: the soldiers go inside the outer letters
take the first and last letters of seaport

explanation.surface: Idiot troops are judged on the edge of a harbour town.
explanation.definitionFit: An evaluation or appraisal, a rating of value or quality.

clue.text: Possible policeman's bid to keep in charge

indicators.note: the word for bid holds the abbreviation inside it

explanation.surface: A constable's attempt to keep control.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of policeman's stands for 'is', linking definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A police constable is addressed as this, though an army rank also fits, hence possible.

clue.text: Dangerous reptile about to top fabulous bird

indicators.note: in a down entry the about letter sits above the bird

parts.note: the roc is a giant bird of legend

explanation.surface: A lethal reptile is set to kill a mythical bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Short informal word for crocodile, a large predatory reptile.

clue.text: Board eastern rescue vessel, holding medical degree

indicators.note: the eastern vessel pair contains the degree letters between them

parts.note: Noah's ark rescued the animals from the flood

explanation.surface: Climbing onto a lifeboat in the east with a doctor aboard.
explanation.definitionFit: To go on board a ship or aircraft, to begin a journey.

clue.text: Gathered in entrance to field, then went astray

indicators.note: the first letter of field, its way in

parts.note: erred means strayed from the right course

explanation.surface: Things collected at a field gate then wandered off.
explanation.definitionFit: Gathered in the sense of concluded or deduced from evidence.

clue.text: He may get into a row transferring charges between banks

definitions.text: He may get into a row transferring charges between banks

parts.words: He may get into a row transferring charges between banks
parts.note: a boatman rows passengers (his charges) across a river from one bank to the other; the surface suggests money moved between financial banks after a quarrel

explanation.surface: Someone moving funds between banks ends up in an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' is rowing a boat, not a quarrel; 'charges' are passengers in his care; 'banks' are riverbanks.
explanation.definitionFit: A boatman who carries people over a river is doing exactly this job.

clue.text: Painter decoratING RESidences in the centre

indicators.note: the letters sit in the middle of the two words, straddling the gap between them

explanation.surface: An artist is busy decorating houses in the middle of town.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean-Auguste-Dominique Ingres was a French neoclassical artist.

clue.text: Bishops collectively cite Pope as misguided

indicators.note: misguided means led astray, so these letters go wrong into a new order

explanation.surface: Church leaders quoting the Pope in a wrong-headed way.
explanation.definitionFit: The body of bishops in a church, taken as a group, is so called.

clue.text: Reversal of gross imperfection in timber

indicators.note: the word for gross is turned round to read backwards

parts.note: rank means gross, flagrant, as in rank stupidity

explanation.surface: Turning over a grossly flawed plank of wood.
explanation.definitionFit: A knot or gnarled lump in wood, a variant of knur.

clue.text: Get mug to wrap last of inferior fabric

indicators.note: the two words placed side by side enclose a letter between them

parts.note: to get something is to see it, understand it
a mug is a gullible person, a sucker

indicators.note: points to the final letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Someone is told to fetch a cheap cup wrapped in poor cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: A puckered striped cotton or linen cloth, often used for summer suits.

clue.text: Bird originally seen with a patron saint of France

indicators.note: take just the first letter of seen

parts.note: St Martin of Tours is one of France's patron saints

explanation.surface: A bird first spotted alongside a French patron saint.
explanation.definitionFit: A small brown swallow-like bird that nests in sandy banks.

clue.text: Shady activity of Greek character involved in retail trade

parts.note: chi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A dodgy Greek in shops pulling a fast one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greek character' suggests a person from Greece; it is a letter of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheating or swindling, a slangy sense of the verb to chisel.

clue.text: Sack race unexpectedly disrupted by his blundering

indicators.note: the first group of letters is broken open by the second
the word race comes out in a surprising new order
the word his stumbles into a different order

explanation.surface: A sack race goes wrong when he trips everyone up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sack race' looks like one phrase, but 'Sack' is the definition; 'unexpectedly' and 'blundering' each scramble their word, and 'disrupted by' splits the first scramble around the second.
explanation.definitionFit: To sack is to dismiss from service, especially an officer in disgrace.

clue.text: Like old staff Mussolini initially addressed in prison

indicators.note: the dictator and the letter go inside the prison word
only the first letter of addressed

explanation.surface: The fascist leader is first spoken to in jail about an ancient rod.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staff' is not employees but a rod: Hermes' snake-entwined wand.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to the caduceus, the herald's wand carried by Mercury in myth.

clue.text: Tasteless cool drink a princess once sent back

parts.note: a sip is a small drink

indicators.note: the princess's short name is returned, read backwards

explanation.surface: A trendy drink once returned by a royal for lacking flavour.
explanation.definitionFit: Bland, lacking flavour or interest; insipid food has little taste.

clue.text: Contract is put together, restricted by this writer's impracticality

indicators.note: the contract words are confined within the writer's letters

parts.note: the setter is this writer, and I'm is short for I am

explanation.surface: A contract is drawn up, though the author finds it unrealistic.
explanation.definitionFit: Pursuing ideals over practical considerations, an unrealistic outlook.

clue.text: Hold forth, disturbing medical

indicators.note: disturbing throws these letters into disorder

explanation.surface: A doctor's examination becomes an unsettling lecture.
explanation.definitionFit: To speak at length in an oratorical, rhetorical way, to orate.

clue.text: Fantasise about private thoroughfare where the current flows

indicators.note: the word for fantasise goes around the others

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: Daydreaming about owning a private road.
explanation.definitionFit: Describes the direction a river's flow takes, further along with the stream.

clue.text: Gain a few points giving description of cold weather?

parts.note: in rugby a try scores five points

explanation.surface: Scoring a little in a game played in chilly conditions.
explanation.walkthrough: A try is rugby's touchdown, worth five points.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjective for frosty, snowy, cold conditions typical of the coldest season.

clue.text: Directions given to robber at first in jug

parts.note: E, W and E, three compass points

indicators.note: take only the opening letter of robber

explanation.surface: A thief is told where to go, ending up in jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jug' looks like slang for prison, where a robber might end up, but here it is a pitcher.
explanation.definitionFit: A large pitcher with a wide mouth, traditionally used with a washbasin.

clue.text: Director caught single mother finally shielding internet pest

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: the letters for single plus a final letter surround the pest

parts.note: a troll posts provocative messages online

indicators.note: take only the last letter of mother

explanation.surface: A single mum is caught protecting an online troublemaker.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who manages or directs an organisation or its operations.

clue.text: Brags endlessly, finding kiln for drying hops

indicators.note: both ends of the word for brags are cut off

explanation.surface: A braggart going on and on about a hop-drying kiln.
explanation.walkthrough: An oast house is a building with a kiln for hops, common in Kent, England.
explanation.definitionFit: The drying kiln itself, as in the oast houses of hop-growing Kent.

clue.text: Three-part poem Tennyson originally delivered outside

indicators.note: use just the opening letter of Tennyson
the word for delivered goes around the poem's title

explanation.surface: A Tennyson poem first delivered as a three-part work.
explanation.walkthrough: The poem is not by Tennyson: 'If—' is Rudyard Kipling's.
explanation.definitionFit: Botanical term for split into three lobes or parts.

clue.text: Urge king to visit a current sporting get-together

indicators.note: the urge and king letters go into the space between the other two pieces

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: Pressing a monarch to drop in on a fashionable event.
explanation.definitionFit: Social gathering of skiers after a day on the slopes, French for after skiing.

clue.text: One girl mostly left backing another's singular marital state

parts.note: Mo, a short form of Maureen

indicators.note: the shortened word is read backwards
the word for left loses its final letter

explanation.surface: One girl has left, mostly to support another, a sorry romantic state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts GONE to GON and 'backing' turns it to NOG; the 's of another's is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Marriage to only one partner at a time, the single-spouse arrangement.
